note:
What people are saying about the two SIDES in each fixture, rather than about individual players.

This exists because club-level commentary is the reasoning most managers actually use — 'Brighton have a strong defence', 'that back three is missing two starters' — and it applies to everyone in the fixture at once. Written into a single player's write-up it reaches a single player, and the app goes on recommending the other ten as though the opposition were neutral.

An attacker gets shown what people say about the opposition DEFENCE. A defender or keeper gets shown what people say about the opposition ATTACK. Everything is attributed; a matchup note without a source is somebody's guess.

Deliberately not derived from fixture-difficulty ratings. FDR is a number, and it flattens exactly the detail that changes a decision — 'a reshuffled back three missing two starters' and 'solid, ranked 8th' can carry the same rating and are not the same problem.

fixtures.headline: A reshuffled Palace back three against Haaland, and a City midfield that is still being built.

defence.point: Palace are without Chadi Riad (knee) and Ismaïla Sarr (groin), so the back three is expected to be Canvot, Richards and Tomiyasu — a reshuffled unit being asked to handle Haaland while Cherki works the space between the lines behind him.

Pierre Sage's 3-4-2-1 is built to be aggressive rather than passive: the first line of pressure pushes the ball wide so the wing-back and wide centre-back can trap it there. That is continuity from Glasner in shape, but it leaves space in behind against a runner.
Selhurst Park on a Friday night is a genuinely awkward place to visit, and this is Palace's best set of conditions all season.

Confirmed on deadline day: Sarr is out with a groin problem that is taking longer than hoped, and Chadi Riad is feared to have a long-term knee injury after being stretchered off in GW1. Kadioglu does return to the matchday squad.
Palace have under a 20% chance of a clean sheet this week — one of the five lowest in the league.

attack.point: Against a City side that has conceded in both of its competitive games and still looks like it is assembling itself, the read is that Palace will get a goal.
Foden, Nico O'Reilly and Semenyo are expected behind Haaland — three creators feeding one striker, which is the shape that has produced his best returns.
Haaland had five shots and two on target at Bournemouth without scoring, including a first-half chance he missed the ball on entirely. The volume was there; the finish wasn't.
Maresca confirmed Doku is out two to three weeks with a calf problem picked up in the Community Shield, and Matheus Nunes is 'not yet 100 per cent'. Bouaddi is available and Elliot Anderson is fine.

defence.point: City's midfield is described as a construction site — Rodri, Bernardo Silva and Reijnders all left in one window and Anderson arrived three weeks ago. They have conceded in both competitive games so far.

fixtures.headline: Anfield has stopped being a fortress against this specific opponent, and Liverpool are missing five.

defence.point: Liverpool have lost their last two league matches against Forest at Anfield — more than they had in the previous thirty meetings there (W24 D5 L1). This is a genuinely bad matchup, not a routine home game.
Andoni Iraola will be without five first-team players for this one.
Liverpool needed a 99th-minute Szoboszlai penalty to draw 2-2 with Newcastle in GW1, having twice come from behind.
Chiesa is unavailable with a small muscle injury picked up against Como.

attack.point: Gakpo and Szoboszlai scored in GW1; the attack functioned, the defence did not.
Liverpool managed 27 shots and 2.98 xG in GW1 and top the projected-goals table over the next three, four and five gameweeks.

defence.point: Forest set up in a 3-4-2-1 with Sels behind Diomande, Milenkovic and Murillo — a settled, physical back three.

Iraola on Forest, unprompted: 'you can see straight away the shape, they don't concede a lot of chances… they defensively are very solid.' The home manager talking up the visiting defence is not nothing.

attack.point: Gibbs-White has scored (2) or assisted (1) three of Forest's last six goals at Anfield, and no player has scored more Premier League goals in the calendar year 2026 than his 12.
Forest have started indifferently under new boss Oliver Glasner, losing 1-0 at home to Leeds to a late Stach free-kick.
Iraola again: 'they have also very good players up front… good threats in the counter.'

fixtures.headline: The reason not to chase Chelsea's Gameweek 1 hauls: Brighton are top of the league and have owned this fixture.

defence.point: Brighton posted their best defensive season in five years last term — 46 conceded, with only Manchester City and Arsenal more watertight.
Hürzeler's side led the entire Premier League for final-third regains (192). He talks about an 'emphasis on defending together', with the striker having 'the mindset of the first defender'.

Brighton have beaten Chelsea in three of the last five meetings, including 3-0 at the Amex in April 2026 and 3-1 at Stamford Bridge in September 2025. They will not be fearful here — they are top of the league.
Won four of their last five, the only dropped points a 0-0 in the Conference League. Preseason clean sheets against Roma (3-0) and Bologna (1-0).
The direct FPL advice: think twice about bringing in Palmer, João Pedro or Rogers this week — Brighton are a completely different proposition to Chelsea's Gameweek 1 opponents.

The counterpoint to Brighton's defensive reputation: the bookmakers give them under a 20% chance of a clean sheet here, one of the five lowest in the gameweek. A good defence at a hard away ground is still a hard away ground.

attack.point: Brighton pressed high against Villa and got their rewards, winning 4-0. A large portion of their attacks funnel down De Cuyper's left flank.
Chelsea won a five-goal West London derby against Fulham with goals from João Pedro, Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer — but the caveat everyone is attaching is the quality of the opposition.

Palmer is the most important player in the side in the No.10 role, and Maresca's positional play has historically put him in favourable central positions and maximised his shooting — a clear system effect rather than pure individual form.
The striker profile keeps changing around him — João Pedro plays as a false nine, Delap is more of a poacher — and Palmer has visibly missed a Jackson-type runner ahead of him.
João Pedro's 11-point haul at Fulham has made him the most-bought forward in the game — 288,000 and counting, nearly twice any other forward.

defence.point: Wesley Fofana misses the first two gameweeks through suspension after a red card late last season.
Chelsea are among five sides above a 30% clean-sheet probability this week.

fixtures.headline: Top of the projections for both goals and clean sheets — against a promoted side that has just won away.

defence.point: A promoted defence adjusting to the top flight, which is the softest fixture profile available in the game.
Ipswich are among the five sides with under a 20% chance of keeping a clean sheet.

attack.point: Ipswich arrive high after a 2-1 win over Sunderland at Portman Road, substitute Jack Clarke scoring a 90th-minute winner. This is not a beaten side turning up.
Ipswich have the LOWEST projected goals of any side in the gameweek at 0.74.
Manchester United are top of the projections for BOTH goals and clean sheets in Gameweek 2.
The plan is defensive stability plus central control through Bruno Fernandes to unlock Ipswich's lines — note the word 'central', which is a deeper brief than his 2025/26 role.
Bruno Fernandes has said he is eager to 'make it right' against Ipswich after being given a bloody nose at Hull.
Manchester United top the Gameweek 2 projections for goals scored at 2.24 — the highest figure in the league.

defence.point: United lost 2-0 at home to promoted Hull in Gameweek 1, which is exactly the result that makes 'they're at home to Ipswich' a less comfortable sentence than it looks.
United also lead the clean-sheet projections at 48%. Only Coventry are also above 40%.

fixtures.headline: The Scout is going all-in on this one — but it is at Villa Park, not the Emirates.

defence.point: Villa Park has become one of the most difficult environments in the division for visiting sides, and Villa won the Europa League and finished fourth last season.
Against that: they were taken apart 4-0 by Brighton on the opening weekend, and João Gomes is suspended after his red card in that game.

attack.point: Villa were beaten 4-0 at home by Brighton in GW1 — the attack did not function.

Ollie Watkins is on his way to Al-Hilal — Villa accepted €58.4m plus bonuses and he travels for a medical this week, with Nicolas Jackson lined up to replace him. Their centre-forward position is mid-transfer.
Fantasy Football Scout's early Scout Picks are 'all-in on Arsenal v Villa' — the most concentrated single-fixture position they have taken this season.
Arsenal opened with a 3-0 win over promoted Coventry at the Emirates.
Saka is fit but Arteta would only say he was 'ready to be involved' when asked whether he could start — he came on as a substitute last weekend after returning late from World Cup duty.
Arteta has been playing Havertz in midfield with Gyökeres up top, which changes who the Arsenal forward pick actually is.
Arsenal are projected to score 1.62 goals, second only to Manchester United. Ödegaard took 11 points and maximum bonus in GW1; Tzolis, who set up seven pre-season goals, assisted Saka.

defence.point: Saliba and Timber were unavailable on the opening day, which puts early-season pressure on Mosquera and White precisely as Villa arrives.
Rotation risk for everyone in that back line outside Gabriel and Raya, now that Konsa has also signed. Calafiori is likely first choice over Hincapié, but he carries more rotation risk than Gabriel.
Arteta said he will assess Calafiori and Hincapié in the final training sessions. Konsa is available after training well.

fixtures.headline: Two promoted sides, and the second-best clean-sheet projection in the gameweek.

attack.point: Coventry are projected to score 1.61 goals — third in the league this week, behind only Manchester United and Arsenal, and comfortably the best fixture outside the big sides.

defence.point: Coventry are the only side other than Manchester United above a 40% clean-sheet probability this week.
They have eleven players priced at £4.0m, the cheapest tier in the game — this is where budget enablers come from if the clean sheets are real.

attack.point: Hull beat Manchester United 2-0 on the opening day through Semi Ajayi and debutant Nobel Mendy. Projected at 0.91 goals here.
attack.source: Hull City official / Fantasy Football Scout

defence.point: Big relief for Hull's £4.0m defenders: Mendy, Ajayi and Giles all had cramp rather than injuries, and Coyle's ankle is an ongoing niggle rather than something new.

fixtures.headline: Marco Rose's first home league game, without the striker who scored 13 last season.

attack.point: Eli Kroupi scored 13 Premier League goals in his debut season — more than any other Bournemouth player — and had foot surgery in July. He is out for three months. That is the attack's main source of goals removed.
Bournemouth publish their own 'FPL: Who to watch in Gameweek 2' preview on the club site.

defence.point: Rose reports no fresh concerns, but Adli (calf), Milosavljevic (knee) and Araujo (thigh) are all medium-term absentees alongside Kroupi. Ryan Christie returns from suspension.
Bournemouth are among the five sides projected above a 30% clean-sheet probability this week — the one genuinely encouraging number attached to them.

attack.point: Everton opened with a 2-0 win over Crystal Palace.

defence.point: A clean sheet against Palace on the opening day. Moyes' press conferences are published in full on the club site if you need late team news.
